note: SPACE-009 protect host edits: src/selfhost/reconciliation.zig compares three versions - the revision the guest started from, the host's current bytes, and the guest's export - and writes only when the host still matches the base, so a guest edit applies exactly when it is the change the host does not have. Both-changed-same is already present, both-changed-differently is divergence reported with the digests of both sides, and the host file is not written: overwriting there destroys work that exists nowhere else and a 'prefer newer' rule is a coin flip dressed as policy. A path the host removed while the guest edited it is divergence too, not a silent recreation that would undo a deletion the user made deliberately; a path new in the guest applies, and the same path produced on both sides with no common base is divergence because without a starting point there is no way to tell an edit from a clobber. Testing found two real gaps rather than confirming the first draft: a new file with no base was reported divergent instead of applied, which the added status now models, and my assertion that a divergent result always carries a host digest was wrong because a host-deleted file legitimately has none. Fault proof: letting the guest always win overwrites the host's divergent file and the unchanged-bytes assertion fails (exit 1); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain.
